title: Study on the Compreflex® Compression Device in the Local Treatment of Venous Leg Ulcers
official: Clinical Investigation of the Compreflex® Compression Device in the Local Treatment of Venous Leg Ulcers: Randomized Non-inferiority Clinical Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical investigation is to compare the Compreflex® adjustable compression medical device with all multi-type compression bandage kits reimbursed in France in patients with venous leg ulcer (VLU). The main question it aims to answer is: Is the adjustable Compreflex® compression device from Sigvaris non inferior to the multi-type bandage kits marketed and reimbursed in France for the treatment of VLU.

Researchers will compare the adjustable Compreflex® compression device to the multi-type bandage kits marketed in France on the complete healing of VLU.

Participants will be randomly allocated to the adjustable Compreflex® compression device or to a multi-type bandage kit, according to the study physican current practice. Then they will be followed-up according to routine patient care, on-site by the study physician and at home by a nurse. Only additional procedures will be added to certain visits:

* Photography of the wound taken by the healthcare providers
* Questionnaires regarding patients quality of life, satisfaction

interventions.name: Multi-type compression bandage kit ROSIDAL SYS
Multi-type compression bandage kit Biflex Short Strech®

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult patient (\> 18 years old)
* Patient with stage C6 or C6R venous leg ulcer (CEAP classification)
* Patients with an Ankle Brachial Index (ABI) \> 0.8 and \< 1.4 or a toe systolic blood pressure (TSBP) \> 0.7
* Patients with a wound that is 1 to 24 months old
* Patients with a wound surface area between 2 and 50 cm²
* Patients available for 12 weeks of follow-up
* Patients able to participate in the study
* Patients who have signed the consent form for participation in the study
* Patients affiliated with a social security system

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient with a necrotic ulcer
* Patient scheduled for interventional treatment of varicose veins or post-thrombotic syndrome in the affected lower limb within the next 3 months
* Patient with ankle systolic pressure (ASP) \< 60 mmHg or toe systolic pressure (TSP) \< 30 mmHg
* Patients with ankle systolic pressure (ASP) \< 60 mmHg or toe systolic pressure (TSP) \< 30 mmHg
* Patients with cancer-related wounds
* Patients with wounds located on the forefoot or thigh
* Patients with peripheral neuropathy
* Patients with a history of superficial or deep vein thrombosis within 3 months prior to inclusion in the study
* Patients with severe heart failure (NYHA class III or IV)
* Patients with scleroderma
* Patients with active cancer (excluding basal cell carcinomas)
* Patients undergoing chemotherapy, long-term immunosuppressive therapy, or long-term corticosteroid therapy
* Patients deprived of their liberty
* Patients unable to sign the consent form for participation in the study
